subject: Hosted API: model v2.3 rollout correlated with P95/P99 latency spikes — customer escalation
messages:
From: Sarah Patel <sarah@brightpath.ai>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: P95/P99 spikes after model v2.3 rollout

Hi Karthik / Lauren,

We rolled model v2.3 in production on Hosted API at ~07:30 PT this morning and immediately started seeing a spike in P95 and P99 latencies for our inference calls. The spike is most visible on our peak traffic windows and we've had 12 customer-facing timeouts in the last 45 minutes.

Attached: latency_trace_v2.3.zip with a 10-minute span of traces, a screenshot of the perf dashboard, and a small CSV of canary metrics.

Quick details:
- Endpoint: POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate (tenant: brightpath)
- Observed: P95 up from ~180ms baseline to 1.2s, P99 up to ~2.6s; error rate increased from 0.2% -> 1.6%
- Throughput: overall TPS steady but request concurrency appears to queue (see traces)

Can you confirm whether the v2.3 rollout included any kernel changes, batching adjustments, or quantization profile swaps? We need to understand risk and an ETA for mitigation -- this is affecting an active demo with one of our enterprise customers.

Thanks,
Sarah
Director of Engineering, BrightPath Analytics

[Attachment: latency_trace_v2.3.zip (zip)]

Thanks for the heads up, Sarah. We're on it.

Initial plan:

- Validate whether autoscaler/cold-start behavior or batching policy changed for the v2.3 rollout (lauren).
- If we see clear regression on the canary, prepare an immediate partial rollback plan for hosted API traffic.

Marcus / Lauren -- I need an initial triage update within 30 minutes. I'll escalate to Hannah if we confirm customer impact beyond our SLOs.

-- Karthik
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: P95/P99 spikes after model v2.3 rollout

Karthik / team -- quick summary of what I see from the canary runs: 

- Correlation: requests routed to v2.3 instances show a bimodal latency distribution. Median ~160ms (same), P95 ~1.1s, P99 ~2.5s. Old model v2.2 P99 remains ~300ms.
- Root cause hypothesis: a new attention-kernel selection path in v2.3 that switches to a slower fused kernel for certain token patterns (observed for inputs with repeated long-tail tokens). It's triggering much more frequent kernel migration (see snippet).
- Additional observation: KV cache hits are unchanged, but continuous batching is falling back to smaller batches on v2.3 due to longer per-request generation time -> effective throughput per-GPU drops under peak concurrency which causes queueing.

Log snippet (anonymized):
[2027-08-21T09:34:12Z] tenant=brightpath model=v2.3 inst=gpux-12 kernel=attn_fused_v3 switch=true seq_len=256 cost=1.9ms
[2027-08-21T09:34:12Z] tenant=brightpath model=v2.3 inst=gpux-12 batch_size=2 effective_lat=1.2s

Next actions I'm running now: full canary comparison of kernel selection counts, run microbench on representative sequences, and prepare a rollback artifact for traffic split revert.

Marcus
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime

Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2027 15:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Action plan & exec note — v2.3 regression (BrightPath)

Folks — final summary and action items after extended triage. Looping in Hannah for executive visibility and Lauren for ops confirmation.

Summary:
- Confirmed regression tied to v2.3 kernel selection path causing long-tail attention executions under certain input patterns. This increased P95/P99 and briefly raised error rates for BrightPath.
- Impact: customer-facing timeouts during demo window; incident created PD-998271.

Action plan (immediate):
1) Roll back host routing for BrightPath tenant to v2.2 (partial rollback) within 30 minutes of this message. Marcus has a rollback artifact staged and a verified runbook.
2) Re-run regressions on a stabilized v2.3 build with kernel flag disabled; if green, we will reintroduce v2.3 behind a stricter canary fraction (0.5%).
3) Customer outreach: Sarah, we'll provide a summary, timeline, and a committed follow-up with root-cause analysis and preventive actions (kernel guardrails). Lauren — please coordinate the customer-facing message and credit approval if applicable.
4) Exec escalation: Hannah, request (if needed) a one-off credit and a short briefing for BrightPath leadership.

I'll start the rollback now and will update once the tenant is on v2.2. Marcus / Lauren — confirm when rollback completes and paste the post-rollback P95/P99 numbers.

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
